scopeRationale: These existing canonical examples were assessed against DR-001 through DR-016. The composition policies are explicitly unassessed here, not passing or inapplicable. Their separate engine calibration does not establish whole-gallery composition conformance.

DR-003.evidence: Reduction values have percent units and shared 12-lane scope.

DR-004.evidence: An empty input is not presented as an observed zero.

DR-005.evidence: Both variants share visual and interaction encodings.

DR-006.evidence: Constraint and validation stay adjacent to the proposed value.

DR-007.evidence: Compact form preserves readable type and usable controls.

DR-008.evidence: Review: decoration does not compete with the editing task.

DR-010.evidence: Review cancellation preserves proposal, scope, and current value; rejection recovery is DR-012's boundary.

DR-011.evidence: Allowed reduction is exposed before commitment and review exposes scope.

DR-012.evidence: Only Bad discards the rejected proposal; guidance and downstream recovery remain identical.

DR-013.evidence: Review: proposal, validation, and corrective action lead the rejected state.

DR-014.evidence: Native labeled controls, focus recovery, associated validation, and keyboard dialog are shared.

DR-015.evidence: Review enlarged text and content variation; no fixed-height task container.

DR-016.evidence: Color does not encode a data variable.

DR-001.evidence: No charts, scale domains, or time-series comparison.

DR-002.evidence: No graphical magnitude encoding; quantities are text.

DR-003.evidence: Fixed labels expose measure, day, snapshot time, scope and units. Both variants retain the same known counts.

DR-004.evidence: Only known observed counts; no missing or estimated values.

DR-005.evidence: The shared accent means attention, not carrier identity, warning severity, selection or success. Review that the swapped emphasis does not invent a status. Executed role-style and text-contrast checks support, but do not settle, that judgment.

DR-006.evidence: Scope, the action and its reason remain local; both sections fit together on desktop, and critical text stays unclipped.

DR-007.evidence: Review bounded widths, legibility and usable actions at both widths; 125% component text is not browser zoom.

DR-008.evidence: Both roles are restrained. Accent and type provide hierarchy without ornamental noise, oversized controls, hidden facts or unreadable supporting text.

DR-009.evidence: Disclosure shows the actual three fixture identities awaiting correction; it does not claim correction or dispatch.

DR-010.evidence: Disclosure preserves scope, counts and invoking focus in both variants.

DR-011.evidence: Review 3 exceptions offers read-only inspection; it does not correct addresses or dispatch shipments.

DR-012.evidence: Read-only inspection, without editable work, consequential submission or failure recovery. Disclosure dismissal is continuity/access.

DR-013.evidence: Good assigns the shared accent and primary type scale to actionable exceptions; Bad assigns them to daily volume. Native style checks reject the old Good and the wrong assignment, but a reviewer still judges task priority.

DR-014.evidence: Real Tab/Enter/Escape sequence, visible focus, ARIA linkage and shared action target. Not full accessibility certification.

DR-015.evidence: Inspect 1200px desktop and 390px narrow captures, including 125% component text and longer guidance. Native clipping/legibility checks supplement human review.

DR-016.evidence: Accent selects the primary presentation role; it is not a category, magnitude, warning or risk color scale. Text and actions retain labels and measured contrast.
